summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired experiment evaluating runtime verifier feedback (co-design) vs static post-hoc verification for LLM-driven NetOps planning. Results show a small but statistically significant absolute increase in safe end-to-end completion (Δ≈+0.0428, exact McNemar p=0.0078125) on 187 complete paired tasks in a deterministic synthetic/emulated corpus. Strong reproducibility artifacts and disclosure are provided. Key limitations concern (a) preregistered secondary/sensitivity analyses and latency diagnostics not reported or inconclusive, (b) use of a shared-initial-generation semantics that affects interpretation and must be discussed explicitly, and (c) single-model and synthetic-emulator scope limiting external validity.
critical_issues: Preregistered sensitivity analysis (treating incomplete pairs as failures) and some preregistered secondary analyses (latency non-inferiority) are not reported as executed; the manuscript must explicitly disclose any unexecuted preregistered analyses and the consequences for confirmatory claims.

The manuscript does not adequately discuss the consequences of the preregistered/shared generation semantics (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate", independent_condition_generation = false) for interpretation of the paired comparison; this design choice can influence observed discordances and must be explained in Methods and Threats to Validity.

Latency non-inferiority hypothesis (H2) was preregistered but is unconfirmed due to missing diagnostics; the manuscript must not imply H2 support and must prominently state that H2 was not executed/confirmed and why.

The paper should include an explicit, concise reproducibility linkage: cite the exact artifact filenames/paths and representative hashes that support each principal numeric claim (complete_pair_count, n_11/n_10/n_01/n_00, bootstrap CI, p-value), to allow deterministic verification from the supplied evidence bundle.
required_revisions: In Methods and Results explicitly state which preregistered analyses were not executed or produced (e.g., the sensitivity analysis treating incomplete pairs as failures and the latency non-inferiority test), explain why they were not produced, and describe the impact on interpretation and confirmatory inference (do not present results for unexecuted analyses).

Add a clear paragraph in Methods describing the generation semantics ("shared_initial_candidate"), justify the choice, and discuss its effect on internal validity and interpretation (including whether guarded runs could re-generate/adapt and how that differs from baseline).

Correctly and prominently label H2 as unconfirmed/inconclusive in the Abstract, Introduction (contributions), Methods, Results, and Conclusion so no reader can infer support for the latency non-inferiority hypothesis.

Add a brief reproducibility mapping (one paragraph or a short table) that links each principal reported number (complete pairs, contingency counts, estimate, CI, p-value) to the specific artifact path(s) and hash(es) in the execution/analysis manifests (e.g., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256: d6a5..., analysis/condition_summary.csv sha256: ef33..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl sha256: 130f6..., execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256: 6a95...).
optional_revisions: If available in the archived artifacts, present the pre-registered sensitivity analysis treating incomplete pairs as failures; otherwise state it as a planned future confirmatory check.

Expand the Threats to Validity to discuss how shared-initial-generation might bias toward conservative or optimistic estimates and include a short rationale for why the observed discordant pattern (n_10=8, n_01=0) is plausible given the design.
Include a concise evidence-to-claim table and the nearest-work comparison matrix within the five-page limit (condensed) to strengthen literature positioning and claim support.
If latency diagnostics now exist in artifacts, include the exploratory latency plot (Figure 2) with numeric summary statistics and note them as exploratory.
